claims.claim: Aristotle born 384 BC at Stagira; joined the Academy at 17 (367 BC); left on Plato's death 348/347; Lesbos c. 345–343; tutor to Alexander 343/342; founded Lyceum 335; left Athens after Alexander's death 323; died at Chalcis 322.
claims.source: Diogenes Laertius V.1–11; Barnes, Aristotle: A Very Short Introduction (2000)

claims.claim: Father Nicomachus was physician to the Macedonian king (Amyntas III).
Surviving works edited by Andronicus of Rhodes, 1st century BC; published dialogues praised by Cicero, now lost.
Four causes (Physics II.3); argument from regularity and the shipbuilding/doctor images (Physics II.8).
Darwin's Historical Sketch note 1 quotes Physics II.8 in Clair Grece's translation.
Darwin to William Ogle, 22 Feb 1882: Linnaeus and Cuvier 'mere schoolboys to old Aristotle' (paraphrased, not quoted).
Aristotle described the hectocotylus arm of the male octopus, confirmed in the 19th century; recognised dolphins as air-breathing and suckling.
claims.source: History of Animals IV.1, V.6, VI.12; Leroi, The Lagoon (2014)

claims.claim: Raphael's School of Athens (1509–11): Plato points up holding the Timaeus; Aristotle palm down holding the Ethics.
Paley, Natural Theology 1802; Aquinas's fifth way; Foot, Natural Goodness 2001; Nagel, Mind and Cosmos 2012; Mayr's 'teleonomy'.
The mean table; bent-stick advice; courage nearer rashness.
Hebrews 5:14 'by reason of use' renders dia tēn hexin, the only NT use of hexis; gegymnasmena = trained.
Kant: virtue and vice differ in kind not degree, against the mean.
claims.source: Metaphysics of Morals (1797), Doctrine of Virtue, Introduction XIII / §10 note

claims.claim: Aquinas: virtue as habitus; theological and infused virtues.
Five intellectual states (episteme, techne, nous, sophia, phronesis).
Equity corrects law in particular cases.
Ambrose names the four cardinal virtues; Aquinas defines prudence as recta ratio agibilium.
claims.source: Ambrose, De officiis I.24; ST II–II q.47 a.2

claims.claim: Anscombe, 'Modern Moral Philosophy' (1958); MacIntyre, After Virtue (1981); MacIntyre converted to Catholicism (early 1980s).
Aristotle's school collected 158 constitutions; Athenian Constitution recovered on papyrus and published by Kenyon in 1891.
Athens had perhaps 30,000 adult male citizens in the 4th century BC.
claims.source: Standard estimates (e.g. M. H. Hansen, The Athenian Democracy in the Age of Demosthenes, 1991)

claims.claim: Friendship: lawgivers care more for it than justice; three kinds.
Best city small enough for one herald; polity and middle class.
Hobbes: humans not political like bees; 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'.
Aquinas: man a 'social and political animal'; government natural even without sin.
claims.source: De regno I.1; ST I q.96 a.4

claims.claim: De Anima II.1 soul definition, axe and eye examples, wax and shape; three kinds of soul; active intellect III.5.
Cicero's endelecheia vs Aristotle's entelecheia question.
Averroes's single intellect; Aquinas's De unitate intellectus (1270).
Unmoved mover moves 'as beloved' (Met. XII.7 1072b3); thought thinking itself (XII.9 1074b34); 47 or 55 movers (XII.8).
Pascal's Memorial (23 Nov 1654), sewn into his coat, names the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, not of philosophers and scholars (paraphrased).
First Vatican Council (1870): God can be known by natural reason.
Natural slave theory; Aristotle's will freed some slaves; Politics VII.10 freedom as reward.
claims.source: Politics I.4–7, VII.10 1330a32–33; Diogenes Laertius V.11–16

claims.claim: Perhaps a third of Athens' population were slaves.
Female as incomplete/deformed male; male supplies form.
Harvey (1651) 'ex ovo omnia'; von Baer identified the mammalian ovum 1827.
claims.source: Harvey, De generatione animalium (1651); von Baer, De ovi mammalium (1827)

claims.claim: Valladolid 1550–51: Sepúlveda (translator of the Politics into Latin) vs Las Casas; Paul III, Sublimis Deus (1537).
claims.source: Hanke, All Mankind Is One (1974); Clayton 2012

claims.claim: Gregory of Nyssa condemns slave-owning, Homily IV on Ecclesiastes (c. 379).
claims.source: Gregory of Nyssa, In Ecclesiasten hom. IV

claims.claim: John Newton, former slave-ship captain, later spoke against the trade and encouraged Wilberforce.
claims.source: Newton, Thoughts upon the African Slave Trade (1788)

claims.claim: Aquinas: woman not defective in God's intention; slavery from sin/human law; all ordered to the same end.
claims.source: ST I q.92 a.1 ad 1; II–II q.57 a.3 ad 2; Supplement q.52 a.1 ad 2

claims.claim: Okin 1979; Williams, Shame and Necessity 1993; Nussbaum capabilities; MacIntyre, Dependent Rational Animals 1999.

Transmission: Boethius; Baghdad translations; Avicenna; Averroes 'the Commentator'; Maimonides' Guide c. 1190; Moerbeke; Paris bans 1210/1215, required 1255; Tempier's 219 propositions 1277; Dante, Inferno IV.131.
claims.source: Rubenstein, Aristotle's Children (2003); Chartularium Universitatis Parisiensis

claims.claim: Luther's Disputation against Scholastic Theology (1517) theses 41–44; Melanchthon restored Aristotle; Leo XIII, Aeterni Patris (1879); Palamas.
claims.source: Luther, WA 1; Melanchthon, Ethicae doctrinae elementa (1550)

claims.claim: Aquinas's relics at the Jacobins, Toulouse, since 1369; Lyceum remains found 1996; San Gregorio, Valladolid, now the National Museum of Sculpture.
Plutarch on Bucephalus and Philip sending for Aristotle.
